[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] XO Communications was a competitive telecommunications carrier providing fiber network and enterprise data services, historically headquartered in Herndon, Virginia. Verizon acquired XO Communications fiber optic network and enterprise business in a transaction that closed in 2016 and 2017, folding its network and facilities into Verizons broader wireline and enterprise operations. Verizon subsequently sold a portfolio of 29 data centers, drawn from its legacy MCI, UUNET, and XO Communications heritage networks among others, to Equinix in a 3.6 billion dollar deal that closed in May 2017, according to contemporaneous press coverage. The XO Fremont facility linked to this operator record, in Alameda County, California, is consistent with this XO and Verizon corporate lineage, though this research did not confirm specifically whether the Fremont facility was among the 29 data centers included in the Equinix transaction or whether it remained with Verizon or another successor. This record is retained under the historical XO name per registry policy against deleting historical operator entries, with the Verizon acquisition and subsequent Equinix divestiture noted here as important context for facility level research to resolve the facilitys current operator. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as Xo Communications Colocation Data Center in Santa Ana, CA, was not individually named in the operator-level research above; its operator field was blank in the source data and is corrected here to XO based on the facility own name, which unambiguously identifies its operator brand. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.
